growth_signal.value: Passed $1B in processed payments in 2025; serves 1,300+ companies a month and about 17,000 workers in 120+ countries; revenue up 25% while costs fell 10%

raised.value: more than $31M, including a $20M Series A led by SoftBank and Tiger Global

entry.idea: Lets a company hire and pay contractors in 150 countries in minutes, with contracts and tax rules handled, while the workers get a global account to receive and spend the money.
entry.lesson: When the giants sell the expensive full package, sell the lighter version the customer actually needs and price it like software.
entry.name: Ontop

growth.reason: Solid but not explosive: revenue up 25% in a year, with the company now focused on margins rather than expansion.

market.reason: Paying remote workers across borders is a worldwide need for companies of every size, and the contractor share keeps growing.

tech.reason: Payments, contracts and compliance plumbing that a strong team can rebuild; rivals like Deel sell similar things.

entry.twist: It skips the expensive employer-of-record model the big players sell and treats the worker as a contractor with their own financial account, from $49 a month.
entry.who_pays: Companies pay a monthly fee per contractor; freelancers get a global account and card.
entry.why_now: The best talent increasingly works as contractors by choice, and companies want to hire across borders without opening a local entity.

mentions.snippet: Lets companies hire and pay workers in other countries with contracts, payments and tax compliance handled.
